text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- A second, $140 million tranche under a funding agreement with the International Monetary Fund sealed in mid-April could be disbursed to Bulgaria within two weeks, the newspaper said without quoting sources.
-- A methane gas explosion injured eleven miners at Bulgaria's Bobov Dol coal mine, the energy committee said. @
-- The cabinet approved draft amendments to the Penal Code aimed at improving legislative base for fighting organised crime, economic crime and corruption.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet decided to unblock 6,000 tonnes of sunflower oil from the state reserves in a move to prevent hoarding by retailers ahead of lifting of price controls from July 1, Trade Minister Valentin Vassilev said.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet decided to sell 22 military industrial plants by year-end under an ambitious privatisation plan aimed to boost the balance of payments, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Bozhkov said.

-- The prosecution said it would demand retracting of the parliamentary immunity of the owner of the ailing Slavyani bank Georgi Agafonov if suspected extending of uncollateralised credits by the bank is supported by evidence. @
The private bank was put in receivership in September 1996 and an insolvency suit was filed by the central bank a month later.
-- Communist-era secret police files of some 400 leading politicians and top judges would be opened by the end of July, head of the parliament's national security commission Hristo Biserov said.

-- The archives of Politbureau, the top ruling body of the Bulgarian Communist Party which was in power for 45 years until November 1989, might be launched on the Internet after being opened, Deputy Prime Minister Vesselin Metodiev said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
